title: Characters of group schemes over arbitrary test schemes and their Laurent values
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $G$ be a $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], and let $T,S$ be $k$-schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Using fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] and the multiplicative group $\mathbf G_m$ [def-sc-gm-ga], put $G_T=G\times_k T$ and $\mathbf G_{m,T}=\mathbf G_m\times_k T$, with their pulled-back group structures. Define the character set $\operatorname{Characters}(G,T)=\operatorname{Hom}_{T\text{-grp}}(G_T,\mathbf G_{m,T})$. For $\chi\in\operatorname{Characters}(G,T)$ and a $k$-morphism $z:S\to G_T$, define its Laurent-coordinate value to be the global section $\operatorname{value}(\chi,z)=(\operatorname{pr}_{\mathbf G_m}\circ\chi\circ z)^*(t)\in\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$, where $t$ is the Laurent coordinate on $\mathbf G_m=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$, with global sections identified by affine spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. These definitions impose no finiteness, commutativity, reducedness or affineness assumption on $G,T,S$.
